findings.reason: as written the node's gate can go green at the base revision on the half of the deliverable that names the defect, and its negative control would be logged as an unbuildable red arm; the plan must either measure the retry that does persist at base (an attempt after the back-off cap elapses, over a span longer than the cap) or drop the attempt arm and make the terminal obligations reason the endpoint.
findings.text: the first case's measurable arm is "over three admission passes the request makes at most one launch attempt", but admission already withholds retries from a request that failed for a reason other than a lane hold: `_retry_backoff_hold` in `reckon/crew/admission/holds.py` leaves the pointer untouched until a bounded back-off elapses and names this exact case in its docstring ("This is what keeps a request that cannot launch — a missing brief, for one — from cycling through a release, a failed dispatch and a restore on every pass"; back-off `30.0`s doubling to a `600.0`s cap in `reckon/crew/admission/shared.py`). So at the base revision three passes inside one back-off window already yield at most one launch attempt, and the head assertion passes unchanged; the declared negative control's red arm ("records a launch attempt on every pass") cannot reproduce, because that per-pass retry is the behaviour the base already suppresses. Only the obligations-reason arm discriminates today, so the node's stated measure of its own headline behaviour ("stops retrying") rests on an instrument that reads the same on both arms.
